verses.1: I say to you, indeed! The one who does not enter through the door into the sanctuary of the priests, but instead returns from another direction, is indeed a thief and a robber.
verses.2: And the one who enters through that door is the shepherd of the sheep.
verses.3: Then the warrior opens the door, hears the sounds of his horse’s voice, and also calls out the names of those horses, thereby bringing them out.
verses.4: When he gives up all his own desires, he moves forward in front of them. The animals follow him, because they know his voice.
verses.5: But they won’t follow the others; instead, they will flee from them, because they don’t know the voice of those who are different from them.
verses.6: This is the meaning of this parable, said Jesus to them. But they did not understand what it meant.
verses.7: So again, Jesus said to them, “I am the door through which people can enter.” I truly say to you that I am that door.
verses.8: All those who came before me were thieves and bandits. But they didn’t listen to the instructions given to them.
verses.9: I am the “door” through which people can enter. Through me, those who enter will be saved, freed from their sins, and will find justice.
verses.10: A thief doesn’t come around unless he wants to steal, sacrifice, and destroy. I came here so that I could have a life and even more than that.
verses.11: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd takes care of his sheep’s souls.
verses.12: The hireling, who isn’t a shepherd at all, doesn’t know how to take care of the sheep properly. He thinks that the wolf will come and take away the sheep, and then he runs away. But in reality, it’s the wolf who steals and eats up the sheep.
verses.13: Because it is a salaried position, and one who works there does not have any responsibilities related to the workers.
verses.14: I am the good shepherd. I will judge those who do me wrong, and I will also be judged by those who do me wrong.
verses.15: Just as my father sees me, so do I see my father. And I place my soul above all other things.
verses.16: And I have other sheep that are not from this flock. I must take them along with me. They will hear my voice, and then they will become one flock, one shepherd.
verses.17: Because of this, my father loves me, because I have given up my soul, so that I can get it back again.
verses.18: No one can deny her from me; I alone can decide whether to give her to someone else or not. I have the right to decide who she should be given to. This commandment was given to me by my father.
verses.19: Again, there was a split among the Jews due to these words.
verses.20: Many of them said that. It’s a demonic thing, and it causes harm. What do you think about that?
verses.21: Others said, “These words are not demonic in nature. It’s impossible for demonic forces to make the eyes of those who are blind see again.”
verses.22: At that time, there were riots in the Holy City. It was winter.
verses.23: And Jesus was also present in the temple, in the house of Solomon.
verses.24: So, the Jews surrounded him and said to him, “When will you give up your soul? If you are indeed the Christ, then tell us.”
verses.25: Jesus replied to them, “Do you not believe what I say? The deeds that I do in the name of my Father bear witness to me.”
verses.26: But you don’t believe that it wasn’t from my sheep.
verses.27: The animals listen to my voice. I know that they will follow me.
verses.28: I give them eternal life. They will not be destroyed in this world, and no one can take them away from me.
verses.29: My father gives me more than anything else. No one can take anything from my father’s hand.
verses.30: I and my father are brothers.
verses.31: Once again, the Jews gathered stones in order to use them as weapons against him.
verses.32: Jesus replied to them, “I have shown you many good things from my Father. Why do you reject some of these things?”
verses.33: The Jews replied to him: “It’s not about good deeds that we’re criticizing you; it’s about your blasphemy. You are acting like you’re a god.”
verses.34: Jesus replied to them, “It is not written in your law, ‘I am God’?”
verses.35: If he said those words to the gods, to whom the word of God was revealed. And it cannot be altered or changed by any means.
verses.36: That man, whom the holy father called and sent out into the world… You say that you mocked him. You said, “I am the son of God.”
verses.37: If I do not carry out the duties of my father’s work, then do not believe me.
verses.38: And if I do, even if you don’t believe in those works, still know and understand that in me there is the Father, and I am part of that Father.
verses.39: So, they tried to catch him again. And he got away from their hands.
verses.40: And he went again across the Jordan to the place where John first baptized. He stayed there.
verses.41: And many people came to him and said that John had done nothing at all. But everything that John said about this was true.
verses.42: And many believed in him there.
